newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden Riksbank sees reduced scope for rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Sweden Riksbank sees reduced scope for rate cuts.

text.p: The deputy governor of Sweden's central bank, Lars Heikensten, said on Tuesday that there was now less room to cut the bank's key repo rate than previously.
"It's clear that when you have cut the rate as much as we have there is not as much room as earlier," Heikensten told a news conference.

The Riksbank cut the repo rate, its key tool for controlling liquidity on the money market, by 10 basis points to 5.05 percent this morning. It has cut the rate 20 times since the beginning of the year when the rate was 8.91 percent.
The Riksbank said earlier on Tuesday in an inflation report that it saw further room for lowering its key repo rate.
Asked if this was a changed signal from the central bank or a new way of saying the same thing, Heikensten said: "Both."
